2027-02-18.title: Second Thursday of the Great Fast
2027-02-18.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The justice and faithfulness of God
2027-02-18.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-18.verse: Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
theo: Paul asks a hard question in today's epistle. If God chose Israel and entrusted them with “the oracles of God”, what happens when some of them prove unfaithful? “What if some were unfaithful? Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? By no means! Although everyone is a liar, let God be proved true.” This is the rock under the whole Great Fast. We come to these weeks aware of promises we have broken: baptismal promises, marriage promises, resolutions made last Lent and forgotten by Easter Tuesday. Our faithlessness is real, but it does not cancel God's faithfulness. He keeps his word when we do not keep ours. The prophet who sat among the ruins of Jerusalem could still say: “The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.”

Paul then refuses a clever argument. Some said: if our sin only makes God's justice and mercy shine more brightly, why not sin more? “Let us do evil so that good may come”? Paul's answer is short: “Their condemnation is deserved!” The Church has kept this as a firm rule of the moral life: we may never do evil so that good may result from it (Catechism 1789). A lie told to save face, a bribe paid to get a good thing done quickly, a small dishonesty in the accounts for the sake of the family: the end does not wash the means. God's mercy is not an excuse for sin; it is the door out of it.

Jesus applies this faithfulness to our ordinary speech. The old law said, do not swear falsely, and fulfil the vows you made to the Lord. “But I say to you, Do not swear at all, either by heaven, for it is the throne of God, or by the earth, for it is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.” We know this speech well in Kerala. “Ammayaane sathyam”, by my mother it is true; “daivathaane”, by God; a hand placed on a child's head to make a word believable. The very need to add an oath shows that our plain word is not trusted. The Church understands that Jesus does not forbid every oath, for an oath may be taken for a grave and just reason, as in a court of law (Catechism 2154). What he asks is that we become people whose word needs no support. “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.” The same is true of the vows and nerchas we make to God in times of need: let them be few, sincere and kept. A fast that makes us more truthful has already begun to make us like God, whose yes is always yes.
outline: Ask: if you said something today without any oath, would people believe you?
Our faithlessness does not cancel his faithfulness.
Point 2 · Not evil that good may come
The end does not wash the means.
By my mother, by God, by my child's head.
Becoming people whose word needs no support.
“Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’.”
live: Do not add “by God” or “by my mother” to anything you say this week; let your plain word stand.
Remember one promise you made and did not keep, and keep it now, or apologise for breaking it.
Look honestly at your work, your accounts and your bills; correct one small dishonesty this Lent.
2027-02-18.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, your Father is faithful even when we are faithless, and his mercies are new every morning. Free us from every lie and from the temptation to do evil so that good may come. Make our speech simple and true, our yes a yes and our no a no, and let our vows to you be sincere and faithfully kept. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana God keeps his promise to be with us always; our Amen at Holy Communion is a yes that should mean yes for the whole day.

quick: Our faithlessness does not cancel God's faithfulness.
We may never do evil so that good may come.
Let your yes be yes and your no be no.
2027-02-18.action: Speak without a single oath today, and keep one promise you have neglected.
2027-02-18.question: Is my plain word trusted at home and at work?

family.explain: Jesus says we do not need to say “I promise on God” or “by my mother” to make people believe us. If we always tell the truth, our yes will be enough. God always keeps his word, and he wants his children to keep theirs.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to tell the truth.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a promise one of us made that we have not kept yet?”

illus: A shopkeeper in Kunnamkulam had a habit of adding “daivathaane” to every price and every promise of delivery. One Great Fast a young customer, half joking, asked him why God had to be brought into the price of rice. The question stayed with him. He decided to stop swearing for the whole of Lent, and found he also had to stop exaggerating, because without the oath the exaggeration sounded empty. Years later his customers say they never bargain with him. They say: when he says it is the last price, it is.

pm.open: Faithful God, your word is true for ever. Make our words true as we pray together. Amen.
share: Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? (Romans 3:3). When have I experienced God's faithfulness after my own failure?
Let us do evil so that good may come? (Romans 3:8). Where am I tempted to justify a small wrong for a good end?
Let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). Where does my speech need more simplicity and truth?
pm.resp: Lord, make our yes a yes and our no a no.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a witness to truth in the world.
For those who give evidence in courts and for all judges and lawyers.
For families broken by lies and broken promises.
For people in business and public life, that they may be honest.
For our group, that our words may be simple and true.
pm.close: Father, your faithfulness is great and your mercies are new every morning. Make us truthful in word and faithful in deed, like your Son, in whom every promise of yours is yes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Saint Paul asks: if some people are unfaithful, does that cancel the faithfulness of God? By no means! Although everyone is a liar, let God be proved true (Romans 3:3–4). We have all broken promises, but God has never broken his.

Paul also rejects a dangerous idea: let us do evil so that good may come (Romans 3:8). The Church teaches that we may never do evil so that good may result. A good end does not make a lie or a bribe right.

Jesus then speaks about our everyday words. Do not swear at all, he says, not by heaven, not by the earth, not even by your own head (Matthew 5:34–36). We know how often we say, by my mother, by God, to make people believe us. Jesus wants us to be so truthful that no oath is needed.
Let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). This Lent, let us keep our promises, speak plainly and truly, and become like our faithful God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says we do not need to say “I promise on God” when we tell the truth. If we always tell the truth, everyone will believe our simple yes or no. Will you try to tell the truth always this week?

q: Ah, you who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

sub: A word that needs no support.
q: O LORD, who may abide in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy hill? Those who walk blamelessly, and do what is right, and speak the truth from their heart;
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
points.apply: Go through this week without a single oath in your ordinary speech.

concl: God's yes never fails, even when our promises do.
Let us become people whose plain word is enough.
2027-02-18.resolve: Keep one neglected promise, and speak without oaths for the rest of the Great Fast.
